name: Cedana
category: other (checkpoint/restore software; not a compute provider)

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Current applicable tariff unverified
plans.note: No public pricing: accounts only via sales/founders contact; demo-led. Commercial licence quoted per GPU (annual) per Cedana's own blog framing; no figure published.

caveats: Live migration and orchestration optimize own GPU infrastructure; public site lacks compute rental price. Software/license pricing and host cost separate; marginal to compute-provider estimator.
Inventory exclusion: migration software for own infrastructure. Card contains no numeric compute modes and no selectable price plan.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Docs expose a 'Cloud Bursting' API (POST /v1/instances with shade_instance_type/shade_cloud, hourly_price per instance type) and a 'Pricing' API where the customer enters their own on-demand/spot $/h per instance type; these are customer-configured cost inputs and brokered third-party instances, not a Cedana public tariff.

snapshot_auto.quote: In short, a job will be automatically checkpointed on preemption and resumed when it starts running again after being re-queued by SLURM (if configured to).
snapshot_auto.note: Checkpoint/restore software you install on your own Kubernetes/SLURM cluster, not a hosted machine. Triggers: SLURM preemption (with GraceTime), policy engine ('heartbeat checkpointing, which will act as a cron job and checkpoint every n minutes', memory-threshold or webhook triggers); on K8s, a rescheduled pod with CEDANA_CHECKPOINT set restores from the latest checkpoint. Process memory (CPU and GPU) plus rootfs diff included. Opt-in per workload via env vars.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Checkpoint via API (see the spec [here](https://demo.cedana.ai/v1/scalar), or just pass this to an agent).
snapshot_on_demand.note: Checkpoint a running pod/job via UI or API; restore on the same or another node ('save the full state of your container enabling you to save, migrate and resume your workloads across instances and vendors'). Memory (CPU+GPU process state) included; restores to new nodes. Container-level, not whole-VM.

fork.quote: You can manually restore the workload on the Checkpoints Page ... you've successfully used Cedana to move a stateful workload between nodes and have it pick up work where it left off.
fork.note: not offered: docs describe restoring a checkpoint to move/resume a workload on another node (migration), not cloning one machine into multiple independent running copies

fork_running.quote: You can manually restore the workload on the Checkpoints Page ... you've successfully used Cedana to move a stateful workload between nodes.
fork_running.note: not offered: no documented capability to clone a still-running workload into a new copy; checkpoints are taken then restored elsewhere

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: you've successfully used Cedana to move a stateful workload between nodes and have it pick up work where it left off.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: checkpoints include memory/process state, but there is no documented fork/clone feature (only single-destination migrate/restore)

pause_resume.quote: To checkpoint a running pod ... You can manually restore the workload on the Checkpoints Page.
pause_resume.note: checkpoint = pause with saved state, restore = resume; core product mechanism for CPU and GPU workloads on the customer's own cluster

wake_on_request.quote: a job will be automatically checkpointed on preemption and resumed when it starts running again after being re-queued by SLURM (if configured to)
wake_on_request.note: not offered: automatic restore is tied to scheduler rescheduling/preemption events, not to an inbound network request waking a sleeping machine

persistent_disk.quote: If you're writing files into the rootfs of the container, we just take them with us on the snapshot! We perform a diff of the filesystem and add it to our process/system-level checkpoint.
persistent_disk.note: rootfs diff plus attached PVCs are captured in the checkpoint and restored, so files survive a checkpoint/restore cycle

volume_attach.quote: If your workload uses PersistentVolumeClaim-backed volumes, Cedana also checkpoints the PVC objects that are attached to the pod ... During restore: Cedana recreates missing PVCs for the restored pod.
volume_attach.note: derived: works through the customer's own Kubernetes CSI/PVC volumes, which Cedana checkpoints and re-attaches on restore

auto_stop_idle.quote: heartbeat checkpointing, which will act as a cron job and checkpoint every n minutes
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: Cedana triggers checkpoints on preemption/policy/cron/webhook events, but does not itself stop machines for idleness since it doesn't host the machines

live_resize.quote: Resize, migrate, and preempt jobs in real time
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; page describes scheduler-level resize/migrate/preempt of jobs across your cluster, not a first-party API to live-resize a single machine's own CPU/RAM
